answer: Give every agent identity two independent harbors to dock at, not one home port. A completed job is replayed in miniature by both harbors, and each harbor emits a signal only if the replay matches the claimed result. Trust grows only when both signals agree; a mismatch strands the job in the meadow between them, open for any third party to inspect. A Sybil farmer can fake one harbor's check by copying a template, but fooling two unrelated replay engines at once costs nearly as much as doing the work honestly, and one exposed fake burns the harbor berths of every identity tied to it.
